solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Settle always has dog across it

indicators.note: the dog lies across the word for always, so its letters wrap around it

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
AY is an old or poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A settlement where something is always accompanied by a dog lying across it.
explanation.walkthrough: AY is an archaic or dialect word for always, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay up is to settle a debt or bill in full.

clue.text: Shook vigorously and questioned persistently

definitions.meaning: first meaning: worked up and down, as when someone pumps a hand

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate senses of one verb in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: One pumps a handle up and down energetically, and one pumps a witness for details by repeated questioning.

clue.text: Bet sketch shows old American dandy

parts.note: a Yankee is a betting term for a combination of eleven bets on four selections
a doodle is an idle sketch

explanation.surface: A wager and a drawing somehow reveal an old-fashioned American fop.
explanation.walkthrough: A Yankee is a British bookmakers' term: a multiple bet covering four horses.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song, Yankee Doodle is the colonial American who stuck a feather in his cap like a macaroni, a dandy.

clue.text: New play put on stage, initially for one with big bill

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of these words are made into something fresh, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to just the opening letter of stage

parts.note: its first letter is S

explanation.surface: A new play is put on at the theatre for someone with a hefty invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PLAYPUT into PLATYPU, and 'initially' adds S, the first letter of 'stage'. 'Bill' looks like an invoice but means a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed platypus has a broad, flat snout shaped like a duck's beak.

clue.text: Two articles on extremely noble goddess

parts.note: A is the indefinite article and THE the definite one

indicators.note: extremely means take only the outermost letters of the word noble

parts.note: its outside letters are N and E

explanation.surface: A pair of articles written about a very aristocratic goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes N and E, the two ends of 'noble', after A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, is the Greek deity of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Turkish officer secures right site for mausoleum

indicators.note: secures means the officer holds the letter for right tightly within

parts.note: an aga was a military commander in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer guards the right place for a grand tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra, in India, is the city where the Taj Mahal, a famous tomb, stands.

clue.text: Argue about a child

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in letter headings
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Parents quarrelling over one of their children.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to put forward a logical case, to argue a point.

clue.text: Set fire to one part of house, which may be brought to court

definitions.text: which may be brought to court

parts.note: lit means set fire to
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gable is the triangular end wall of a house

explanation.surface: An arsonist torches a section of a home, which may well end up as a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigable matter is one that can be the subject of a lawsuit.

clue.text: Ruins meals for Scottish celebrations

parts.note: burns, as a fire does, ruins or destroys
suppers are evening meals

explanation.surface: Someone spoils the food meant for Scottish festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns Suppers are held on 25 January to honour the poet Robert Burns, with haggis and whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: These are annual Scottish dinners commemorating the national poet's birthday.

clue.text: Comic book contributing to human gaiety

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cartoon book adds to people's cheerfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Manga are Japanese comics and graphic novels.

clue.text: Unfortunately shut, a sure store of knowledge

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A library of learning is, regrettably, closed for certain.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is literally a treasury, a collection of words arranged by meaning.

clue.text: Perish, failing to finish slimming programme

indicators.note: failing to finish means the word stops short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a diet is a regime for losing weight

explanation.surface: A dieter who gives up before the end might feel they would rather perish.
explanation.definitionFit: To die is to perish, to stop living.

clue.text: Wastes no time and acts to start machine?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: pushes the On button, literally

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical literal reading of the phrase as pushing a switch.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on resolutely is the idiom; the playful sense is depressing the On switch.

clue.text: African takes Europeans through short canal

indicators.note: through means the Scandinavians pass right inside the shortened waterway
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea
Danes are people from Denmark

explanation.surface: An African guides Europeans along an abbreviated canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is the Suez Canal in Egypt, which fits the African setting of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sudanese person comes from Sudan, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Person so organised departs — for such a walk?

indicators.note: organised means the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: An organised charity walker sets off on a fundraising stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsored walk is a charity event where backers pledge money for each mile completed.

clue.text: Adder, and when to see it?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who sums, adds figures up
second meaning: the season when an adder, the snake, is out and about

explanation.walkthrough: 'Adder' reads as the snake, but one sense is a person who adds; the snake sense then sets up the season when it is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes such as the adder are active in the warm months; one who totals numbers is literally a summer.

clue.text: No good in growing grape

indicators.note: no means the letter for good is absent from the word

parts.note: raising crops means growing them

explanation.surface: Bad news for a vine: nothing good comes from cultivating grapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, and raisin is the French word for grape.

clue.text: Machine gun that sounds as if it is leaking?

indicators.note: sounds as if tells us the entry is spoken like a word meaning dripping

parts.note: oozy means seeping or leaking liquid

explanation.surface: A gun that, by its name, seems to be dribbling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uzi is an Israeli-designed submachine gun.

clue.text: At home quiet, we hear: drop in

indicators.note: we hear tells us the entry is spoken like those words together

parts.note: in means at home; still means quiet and calm

explanation.surface: A neighbour, home and quiet, hears someone dropping round.
explanation.walkthrough: IN STILL said aloud gives the entry, spelt with one L.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil is to introduce gradually, literally to put in drop by drop.

clue.text: No bad notice returned to me for disc

indicators.note: returned means the string from the first three words goes back to front

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A pleasing note arrives saying the disc is fine after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NOILLAD into DALLION, which follows ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a large medal or round, disc-shaped ornament.

clue.text: Rule on new garden feature

parts.note: a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A regulation about a fresh addition to the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is the mown grassy area in a garden.

clue.text: Level time in race perhaps

parts.note: even means level

explanation.surface: Runners neck and neck at the finishing time of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is one example of a sporting event, a competition on a programme.

clue.text: Flower lies tangled with weeds

indicators.note: tangled means the letters are twisted together and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bloom lies in a garden snarled up with weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white alpine plant, a national emblem of Switzerland and Austria.

clue.text: Artist may work at this line, simplicity coming first

indicators.note: coming first means the word for simplicity is placed ahead of the letter for line

parts.note: ease means simplicity, lack of difficulty

explanation.surface: A painter's work may favour clean lines, with simplicity above all.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the wooden stand holding a painter's canvas.
